title: [tools] Generated list of elements in spec missing spaces & punctuation on copy & paste
body:
(Sorry if there's a better repo for this; I assume it affects all specs using the WHATWG spec generator.)

Many parts of the spec use lists with class `brief category-list` which are marked up as `<ul>` and `<li>` but are displayed as comma-separated prose lists using CSS.  While this looks fine, and should be readable but verbose for screen readers, it falls apart if you copy & paste the text. Both Firefox and Chromium browsers strip the CSS-generated content from the text, but do respect the inline display type on the list elements, so that the result is keywords smushed together without spaces or punctuation:

> buttonfieldsetinputobjectoutputselecttextareaimgform-associated custom elements

The browser behavior is, I believe, consistent with the [`innerText` algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#the-innertext-idl-attribute).

Examples: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#categories (the lists of elements in each category that are indicated with an arrow). 

If there are reasons to keep the `<ul>` & `<li>` markup for these compact lists, I would recommend at least including the commas and spaces in the HTML, rather than as CSS generated text.
